draft.title: Adding government, finance and the overseas sector
card: The two-sector model has only households and businesses. The five-sector model adds three more sectors to match a real economy.
Households and businesses pay taxes to the government. The government spends money on things such as schools, roads and hospitals.
Banks and similar bodies collect savings from households. They lend money to businesses, which use it to invest in equipment and buildings.
Households and businesses buy imports from other countries, so money flows out. Other countries buy exports, so money flows in.
draft.remember: Each new sector links to the flow in two directions: money goes to it and comes back from it.

a.q: Which pair of flows links households and businesses to the financial institutions sector?
opts: Savings in, and loans out to businesses
Taxes in, and public services out
Wages in, and goods and services out
a.why: Financial institutions collect savings and lend to businesses that want to invest. Taxes and public services link to the government. Exports and imports link to the overseas sector.
a.clue: Think about where a bank gets money and where it sends it.

b.q: Sam's Surfboards in Torquay sells boards to a shop in Hawaii. Which sector does the money come from, and what is this flow called?
opts: The overseas sector, as an export
The overseas sector, as an import
The government sector, as a tax
b.why: The buyer is in another country, so the money comes from the overseas sector. Goods sold abroad are exports. An import would be the opposite: Australians buying goods from abroad.
b.clue: Who is buying the boards, and where are they?

wants.brief: A five-sector circular flow diagram with boxes for Households, Businesses, Government, Financial institutions and Overseas sector. Arrows show wages, goods and services between households and businesses, taxes to and spending from government, savings to and loans from financial institutions, and imports and exports with the overseas sector. Each arrow is labelled.
wants.why: Seeing all five sectors and their flows together shows how the model builds on the two-sector loop.
